_about: AI-generated settings file: written with an AI assistant (Claude) during the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 hackathon. It describes where NASA's BASS-II video overlay sits and how video/read_overlay.py reads it. Readings made with it are transcribed by code that an AI assistant wrote; not a NASA data file; not reviewed by a person beyond the by-eye samples named in video/README.md. "By eye" means that an AI assistant (Claude) looked at each frame image and wrote the numbers down before it saw the reader's values. No person has checked a frame.
disclosure: Transcribed by code that an AI assistant wrote; not a NASA data file; not reviewed by a person beyond the by-eye samples named in video/data/team_transcription_bass2_onscreen_readings/README.md. "By eye" means that an AI assistant (Claude) looked at each frame image and wrote the numbers down before it saw the reader's values. No person has checked a frame. Checked only on the 19 BASS-II clips named in video/settings/bass2.json.

experiment.name: BASS-II
experiment.title: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II
nasa_documents_used: PSI-25_Science Documents_BASS-II_ReadMe.docx (short phrases and paraphrases in fields[].nasa_readme)

psi.listing: POST {base_url}/files/v2 with JSON {folder: '<accession>/', fileType: 'study', studyId: '<accession>', version: <investigation version>, obfuscationcode: ''}
psi.download: GET {base_url}/studies/<accession>/download?file=<file>&version=<file version>&redirect=false returns a signed link

sampling.note: One frame per second: ffmpeg's fps=2 filter is applied and every second frame it emits is kept (t = 0, 1, 2, ... s). This is the frame choice of the checked pilot; ffmpeg's fps=1 filter picks different frames, so it is not used.

strip.note: Frame pixels. Only this strip of each frame is used; the rest of the picture is never read.

grid.note: Fixed-pitch character grid. Cell k of a line starts at frame column x0 + k * pitch; x0 is measured per clip and frozen in the reader state (159.0 to 161.25 px for these 19 clips). frame_px_box_at_x0_160 in each field is [left, top, right, bottom) in frame pixels at x0 = 160, for reading only.

origin_search.note: Used only for a clip the reader state has no x0 for: maximise mean(on) - mean(off) of the clip-averaged header line.

matching.note: Each cell is compared (normalised correlation, every shift in shift_px in x and y) with every template. The best character is kept when its correlation >= min_corr and beats the best other character by margin. Otherwise the cell is blank if its mean is below ratio x the mean of the header reference cells, else unreadable. A field with any blank inside or any unreadable cell, or whose text does not match its format, is left empty.

overlay_present.rule: overlay_present = mean(on cells) > factor * mean(off cells) + offset, on the header line (FUEL AIR FAN RAD)
overlay_present.missing_overlay: Rule for a missing overlay: overlay_present is reported, but values are not erased because of it. Each field must pass its own character test, which fails on the still-camera screen, blue screen, colour bars or black, so those rows come out empty. Known weakness: on 7 rows (B21 0, 163, 164 s; O8a 80, 81 s; O19 988 s; P5 1608 s) the overlay is on screen over a bright picture, overlay_present is False, and only the fields that passed their own test (RAD, clock, on O19 also FUEL and AIR) are filled.

fields.note: Copied as shown. The NASA documents held by the team do not say what FUEL measures in these solid-fuel tests.

nasa_readme.quote: flow speed measured in the duct
nasa_readme.paraphrase: in cm/s, on the video display; response time about 1 min, so the reading is steady only after a long time at one flow setting
on the video display; maximum 122, that is 12.2 V
the radiometer is shown on the video; gain adjusted to avoid saturation; useful for relative readings; video display data rate 5 Hz

fields.note: Only the first three characters (d.d) are read. The second decimal sits in cell 19, which the right edge of the picture cuts; the value is therefore cut, not rounded.

nasa_readme.quote: one day later than actual date
nasa_readme.paraphrase: the video display date is off by one day because the on-board computer missed a leap year; ISS runs on GMT

fields.note: Six digits HHMMSS written only when all six are read and form a valid time (hours < 24, minutes and seconds < 60). The date on the same line is not read.

clock_check.rule: Offset = clock seconds - t_video_s on every row with a clock; a row is on the line when its offset is within tolerance_s of the clip's median offset. Used by the flag rules and reported per clip. A clock that passes midnight inside a clip is not handled.

flags.reason: NASA's ReadMe gives 122 as the maximum; the screen itself shows 123 to 125 in 16 rows that were checked by eye (by an AI assistant; no person has checked a frame). A higher value is a frame caught while the display was changing (O9 576 s shows 198, between 98 and 102). The value is kept as shown and flagged.

A clock value off the line while the rows just before and after are both read and on the line is a frame caught while the clock was changing (O11 923 s shows 14:45:59 between 14:44:59 and 14:45:00; P22b 411 s shows 16:57:29 between 16:57:19 and 16:57:20). The first and last rows of a clip are never flagged by this rule.

reader_state.note: Path relative to this settings file. Frozen templates (one normalised 14 x 22 pixel image per template, with its character) and the grid origin x0 of each clip. The reader checks the SHA-256 and stops if it differs; it never clusters again.

build.source: the pilot's reader state: x0.json, clusters.npz (K=48, random_state=0), clusters2.npz (K=32, random_state=0); not shipped
build.note: Cluster ids were labelled during the pilot by an AI assistant (Claude) that looked at montages of real cells; no person has checked the labels. A template is the mean of the cluster members whose correlation with the cluster centre exceeds member_min_corr, kept only with at least min_members such members. The ids refer to those exact cluster files: re-clustering would renumber them.
